title: Thrown
html:
For an explanation of all weapon properties, see Weapons.

 Thrown is a weapon property that allows a weapon to be used as a projectile with the  Throw or  Enraged Throw actions.

A melee weapon with this property can be thrown for a ranged attack, and benefits from the creature's Ability Score Modifier (Strength) and Proficiency Bonus as usual, instead of being treated as an Improvised Weapon. This combines with the Finesse property: if throwing a Dagger, which has both Thrown and Finesse, the thrower's Dexterity Modifier may be used for the damage roll, though the Strength modifier is still used for the attack roll.

List of thrown weapons

  •  Daggers
  •  Handaxes
  •  Javelins
  •  Light Hammers
  •  Spears
  •  Tridents

Unique thrown weapons

The weapons listed below possess the Thrown attribute, while other weapons of their same type typically do not.

  • Dwarven Thrower - Warhammer +2
  • Orphic Hammer - Warhammer +3
  • Returning Pike - Pike +1

Weapons that interact with throwing

  • Bloodthirst - When thrown, returns to the owner due to its permanent Bound Weapon condition.
  • Comeback Handaxe - When thrown, returns to the thrower and damages them.
  • Dwarven Thrower - When thrown, returns to the owner. If thrown by a Dwarf (or a character  disguised as one) it deals an extra 1d8⁠⁠Bludgeoning damage - or 2d8⁠⁠Bludgeoning if the target is Large, Huge or Gargantuan.
  • Lightning Jabber - When thrown, deals an additional 1d4⁠⁠Lightning damage.
  • Nyrulna - When thrown, deals 3d4⁠⁠Thunder damage in a ⁠6 m (20 ft) blast, and returns to its owner.
  • Returning Pike - When thrown, returns to its owner.
  • Slinging Shoes - While arguably not a weapon proper, this item - when thrown - deals an additional 2d4⁠⁠Psychic damage, and returns to its owner.

Character features that interact with throwing

  •  Tavern Brawler - Adds damage to thrown items equal to the thrower's Strength modifier

Temporary sources of the Thrown property

Any weapon can be given the Thrown property in two ways:

  • By the  Weapon Infusion magical effect, which is a possible outcome of the Wild Magic Barbarian Wild Magic table.
  • By using  Elemental Cleaver as a Giant Barbarian.

Related items

+1 to Throw Attack Rolls

  • Marksmanship Hat

+1d4 to Throw Damage

  • Gloves of Uninhibited Kushigo
  • Ring of Flinging
  • Shadow-Cloaked Ring - against Lightly or Heavily Obscured creatures and creatures made of shadow

+1d4 to 'Thrown' Weapon Damage

  • Dark Justiciar Gauntlets (Rare) - ⁠Necrotic
  • Dark Justiciar Gauntlets (Uncommon) - ⁠Necrotic
  • Flawed Helldusk Gloves - ⁠Fire
  • Strange Conduit Ring - ⁠Psychic if the wearer is concentrating

+1d6 to 'Thrown' Weapon Damage

  • Helldusk Gloves - ⁠Fire

+2 to 'Thrown' Weapon Damage

  • Caustic Band - ⁠Acid
  • Legacy of the Masters
  • Horns of the Berserker - ⁠Necrotic if the wearer does not have full health

Related character features

  •  Duelling - Adds 2 damage to Thrown weapons when equipped with an appropriate "duelling" weapon

Notes

  • In most cases, unless explicitly stated in a weapon's properties (e.g., the 1d4⁠⁠Lightning damage from the  Lightning Jabber), additional damage found inherently on weapons with the Thrown property, such as the 1d4⁠⁠Radiant damage on the  Shining Staver-of-Skulls, does not apply when thrown; however, additional weapon damage from other sources, such as the 1d6⁠⁠Fire damage from the  Helldusk Gloves, applies to thrown weapons. Similarly, weapon coatings appear to have no effect on thrown weapons.
  • Throwing a weapon with both the Thrown and versatile properties will always deal one-handed damage regardless of whether it was wielded in one hand, wielded in both hands, or thrown from inventory.

Bugs

  • When initiating combat with a character using a returning throwing weapon, it does not trigger the returning property. This only triggers once they are actively in turn-order.
  • Throw attacks use an attack roll of RangedUnarmedAttack, which triggers IsUnarmedAttack() and IsRangedUnarmedAttack(). One result of this is that, in many cases, throw attacks trigger effects which are described as only affecting unarmed attacks.
  • Throwing weapons when dual wielding interacts with fighting styles in the following way: the fighting style applied depends on the weapon that is not thrown and remains equipped. For instance, if a trident and a dagger are equipped (using the  Dual Wielder feat), throwing the dagger can apply  Great Weapon Fighting, since the trident is equipped as a two-handed weapon. On the other hand, if the trident is thrown, the damage bonus from  Duelling can apply.
    • For a melee fighting style to apply, the weapon that is thrown must be equipped in the main hand, and the melee weapon set must be active when throwing. Specifically, the game checks what weapon is in the throwing character's hands when the attack connects with its target, but when throwing a weapon from the off-hand, a character automatically switches from their melee weapon set to their ranged weapon set, inhibiting the bonuses from melee fighting styles. If a character has no ranged weapons equipped, then they receive the effects of melee fighting styles when throwing weapons from either hand.
